To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BRAF and MEKF inhibitors are effective in patients with BRAF mutant melanoma, however, acquired resistance is common and mechanisms of resistance are complex and include genetic and epigenetics alterations.
BRAF inhibitors have a profound impact on the immunosuppressive microenvironment and that this may be one of the mechanisms that contribute to their clinical efficacy.

the BRAFV600E mutation is the most commonly found mutation in melanoma and that the FDA has approved BRAF inhibitors, MEK inhibitors, and combined BRAF/MEK inhibitors as targeted therapy for patients with advanced melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, highly effective, and safe targeted agents to treat melanoma patients.
the development of new therapeutic agents that target specific pathways and mechanisms of resistance to current targeted therapies.
the development of new and more effective therapies for melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of BRAF and/or MEK inhibitors with immunotherapy is an exciting new field that is currently undergoing clinical testing.
BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination therapy has become the new standard of care for BRAFV600 mutant metastatic melanoma.
there are multiple mechanisms of resistance to targeted therapy, including BRAF and MEk inhibitors in melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRAF and MEKP inhibitors are the mainstay of therapy for BRAFV600 mutant melanoma.

we have shown that the combination of BRAF and PI3K inhibitors can be a very effective treatment strategy in BRAF mutant melanoma, and that this strategy may be more effective than the current FDA approved combination of a BRAF and a MEK inhibitor.
the combination of targeted therapy with checkpoint inhibitors is the future of melanoma therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are multiple mechanisms of resistance to combined BRAF and MEk inhibitors and that the use of these inhibitors in combination with immunotherapy or other targeted therapies may overcome some of these mechanisms of resistance.
there are several mechanisms of resistance to single-agent BRAF inhibitors and dual BRAF and MEF inhibitors.

the development of BRAF inhibitors has led to a paradigm shift in the treatment of metastatic melanoma and has provided an opportunity for further investigation of combination strategies to enhance clinical outcomes in patients with advanced melanoma.
